fasti.note: Statius Priscus takes Artaxata.
Verus marries Lucilla at Ephesus.
Avidius Cassius sacks Seleucia and Ctesiphon; the 'Antonine plague' (probably smallpox) breaks out in the army and spreads west (165-166 onwards). Death of Peregrinus at Olympia.
Verus' Parthian triumph. Langobardi and Obii cross the Danube (166/167). Embassy from 'Andun' (Antoninus) reaches China per the Hou Hanshu.
Marcomannic Wars begin (167 or 168). Gold mines of Dacia attacked.
Marcus and Verus at Aquileia; plague in the army.

Lucius Verus dies at Altinum (January/February). Auction of palace treasures to fund the war. Marcomanni and Quadi invade Italy and besiege Aquileia (170 by the usual chronology), the first invasion of Italy since the Cimbri.
Costoboci raid Greece as far as Eleusis (170 or 171).
Only the cognomina are securely known for this pair in dating formulae; fuller names omitted. 'Rain miracle' against the Quadi (172 or 174) depicted on the Column of Marcus Aurelius.
Pompeianus, Syrian-born marshal and second husband of Lucilla.
Marcus writes the Meditations on campaign (c. 170-180).
Revolt of Avidius Cassius in Syria and Egypt after a false report of Marcus' death; killed after three months. Death of Faustina at Halala. Pertinax suffect consul (c. 175).
Marcus founds chairs of philosophy at Athens. Joint triumph with Commodus (23 December).
Commodus made Augustus. Martyrs of Lyon and Vienne (Eusebius, HE 5.1). SC de pretiis gladiatorum minuendis (Italica and Sardis copies, 177).
Constitutio Orfitianum on mothers' succession dated by this Orfitus (SC Orfitianum, 178). Marcus and Commodus return to the Danube.
Laugaricio inscription (Trenčín, Slovakia) of Legio II Adiutrix, 179.

consuls: Lucius Fulvius Rusticus Gaius Bruttius Praesens
fasti.note: Marcus dies at Vindobona or Sirmium (17 March); Commodus makes peace on the Danube. Martyrs of Scillium (17 July), the earliest Latin Christian document.
Conspiracy of Lucilla and Quadratus.
Perennis praetorian prefect dominates (182-185). Victories in Britain (Ulpius Marcellus, 184).
Fuller names uncertain. Perennis lynched at the demand of a deputation of 1,500 soldiers from Britain; Cleander rises. 'Deserters' war' of Maternus in Gaul (186/187).
Fuller names uncertain (Seius Fuscianus, Marcus Servilius Silanus).
Cleander sells 25 consulships for 190 (Dio 73.12).
Grain riot leads to the fall and execution of Cleander. Twenty-five suffect consuls in one year (Dio).
Fire destroys the Temple of Peace with Galen's books (191 or 192).
Commodus renames Rome Colonia Commodiana and the months after his titles; fights as a gladiator. Strangled by the athlete Narcissus (31 December).

Year of the Five Emperors: Pertinax (killed 28 March), Didius Julianus buys the throne at auction (killed 1 June), Septimius Severus proclaimed at Carnuntum (9 April); Pescennius Niger in Syria, Clodius Albinus in Britain (made Caesar). Severus replaces the praetorians with legionaries.
Niger defeated at Cyzicus, Nicaea and Issus; killed. Syria divided into Coele and Phoenice.
Severus' first Parthian war; province of Osrhoene/Mesopotamia. Severus declares himself son of Marcus Aurelius and renames his son Antoninus (Caracalla).
Byzantium falls after a three-year siege. Albinus proclaims himself Augustus. Caracalla made Caesar.

Battle of Lugdunum (19 February): Albinus defeated and killed; Lugdunum sacked; 29 senators executed. Second Parthian war: Ctesiphon sacked (late 197 or January 198). Legionaries permitted to marry (soon after).
Caracalla made Augustus (28 January), Geta Caesar. Mesopotamia a province with two legions (I and III Parthica). Hatra besieged twice in vain (198-199).
Severus in Egypt (199-200); Alexandria given a council.
Tertullian writing at Carthage. Legionary pay raised by Severus (from 300 to perhaps 400-450 denarii).
Caracalla (Marcus Aurelius Antoninus) marries Plautilla, daughter of the praetorian prefect Plautianus. Severan family returns to Africa (202-203); Lepcis Magna rebuilt.
The Geta of this year is the emperor's brother. Arch of Septimius Severus in the Forum dedicated. Martyrdom of Perpetua and Felicitas at Carthage (7 March).
Ludi Saeculares (Severan computation; inscription of the Acta).
Plautianus killed in the palace (22 January). Papinian praetorian prefect.

consuls: Marcus Nummius Umbrius Primus Senecio Albinus
fasti.note: Bandit Bulla Felix active in Italy (206-207).
Severus and his sons go to Britain for the Caledonian campaigns (208-211).
Geta made Augustus (209 or 210).
Severus dies at Eboracum (4 February), advising his sons to enrich the soldiers. Caracalla murders Geta in their mother's arms (26 December 211); damnatio memoriae; Papinian executed.
Constitutio Antoniniana extends citizenship to almost all free inhabitants (P. Giss. 40; dated 212). Asper and his son as joint consuls.
Caracalla's campaign against the Alamanni, their first appearance in the sources. Balbinus the future emperor (238).
Antoninianus (double denarius) introduced (215).
Massacre of the youth of Alexandria by Caracalla.
Baths of Caracalla dedicated (216). Parthian campaign.
Caracalla murdered near Carrhae (8 April); Macrinus, praetorian prefect, proclaimed, the first equestrian emperor. Battle of Nisibis; peace bought from Artabanus V for 200 million sesterces.
Elagabalus proclaimed at Raphanaea (16 May); Macrinus defeated near Antioch (8 June) and killed. Elagabalus took over Macrinus' consulship.
Elagabalus arrives in Rome with the sacred stone of Elagabal of Emesa.
Comazon, former actor and praetorian prefect, consul; Elagabalus marries the Vestal Aquilia Severa.
Severus Alexander adopted as Caesar.
Elagabalus and his mother Julia Soaemias killed by the praetorians (11 or 13 March); Severus Alexander accedes under Julia Maesa and Julia Mamaea. Ulpian praetorian prefect.

consuls: Lucius Roscius Aelianus Paculus Salvius Julianus
fasti.note: Marius Maximus, the biographer of the emperors. Ulpian killed by praetorians (223 or 228).
Ardashir defeats Artabanus IV at Hormozgan (28 April 224): end of the Arsacids, rise of the Sasanians.
Aqua Alexandrina built.
Cassius Dio the historian holds his second consulship with the emperor, then retires to Bithynia because the praetorians threatened him.
Ardashir invades Mesopotamia.
Severus Alexander's Persian expedition (231-233).
Dura-Europos synagogue paintings dated 244/245; house-church c. 232.
Pupienus the future emperor (238). Alamanni cross the Rhine.
Severus Alexander and Mamaea killed by soldiers near Mogontiacum (March); Maximinus Thrax proclaimed. Beginning of the 'crisis of the third century' (235-284).
Maximinus campaigns in Germany (Harzhorn battlefield, Lower Saxony, discovered 2008, dated c. 235-236).

Year of the Six Emperors: Gordian I and II proclaimed in Africa (January-March), killed at Carthage; the Senate's Pupienus and Balbinus; Maximinus killed at Aquileia; Pupienus and Balbinus murdered by praetorians; Gordian III sole emperor. Goths and Carpi sack Histria.
Revolt of Sabinianus in Africa; Legio III Augusta disbanded for its part in 238. Shapur I co-ruler; Hatra falls to the Persians (240/241). Mani begins preaching.
Timesitheus praetorian prefect; Gordian marries his daughter Tranquillina.
Gordian's Persian expedition; temple of Janus opened. Fuller nomenclature omitted where uncertain; third-century ordinarii are often known only from dating formulae (cognomina).
Battle of Rhesaina: Romans defeat Shapur. Timesitheus dies.
Gordian III dies after the battle of Misiche (Persian version, Res Gestae Divi Saporis) or murdered at Zaitha (Roman version); Philip the Arab makes peace for 500,000 aurei.
Philip campaigns against the Carpi.
Philip's son made Augustus.
Millennium of Rome celebrated (21 April 248) with secular games. Revolts of Pacatianus on the Danube and Iotapianus in the East.
Decius proclaimed by the Danubian army; Philip killed near Verona (September). Goths under Cniva invade.
Decius' edict requiring universal sacrifice; libelli from Egypt survive. Pope Fabian martyred (20 January). 'Plague of Cyprian' (c. 249-262).
Battle of Abritus (June/July): Decius and Herennius killed by Cniva's Goths, the first emperor to fall to a foreign enemy. Trebonianus Gallus accedes.
Shapur I takes Armenia; defeats a Roman army at Barbalissos (252 or 253).
Aemilian proclaimed in Moesia; Gallus and Volusianus killed at Interamna; Aemilian killed at Spoletium; Valerian accedes with his son Gallienus. Antioch sacked by Shapur (253 or 256).
Dura-Europos falls to the Persians (256/257), with siege mines and gas warfare evidenced archaeologically. Frankish and Alamannic raids.
Valerian's first edict against Christians.
Second edict: Cyprian of Carthage (14 September) and Pope Sixtus II executed.

Fuller nomenclature omitted where uncertain; third-century ordinarii are often known only from dating formulae (cognomina). Juthungi invade Italy; defeated near Augsburg (Augsburg victory altar, 260).
Valerian captured by Shapur I near Edessa; Gallienus sole emperor, ends the persecution. Postumus founds the Gallic Empire; Macrianus and Quietus in the East; Ingenuus and Regalianus on the Danube.
Odaenathus of Palmyra crushes the Macriani and Quietus. Postumus' consuls in the Gallic Empire run separately (260-274).
Odaenathus invades Persia, reaches Ctesiphon. Temple of Artemis at Ephesus burned by Goths.
Heruli sack Athens (267/268), repelled by Dexippus. Odaenathus murdered; Zenobia rules for Vaballathus.
Gallienus killed at the siege of Milan (September); Claudius II accedes; Goths defeated at Naissus (268 or 269).
Victory over the Goths at Naissus earns Claudius the title Gothicus. Postumus killed; Victorinus in Gaul. Zenobia's forces occupy Egypt (270).
Claudius dies of plague at Sirmium; Quintillus briefly; Aurelian accedes. Antoninianus silver content falls to around 2-5%.

Juthungi and Alamanni invade Italy; Roman defeat at Placentia, victories at Fanum Fortunae and Ticinum. Aurelian begins the walls of Rome (19 km, completed under Probus). Riot of the mint workers. Dacia evacuated (c. 271-275).
Aurelian defeats Zenobia at Immae and Emesa; Palmyra taken; Zenobia captured. Death of Shapur I (270 or 272).
Palmyra revolts again and is sacked. Firmus in Egypt. Tacitus the future emperor.
Tetricus surrenders at Châlons: Gallic Empire reabsorbed. Aurelian's triumph; coinage reform (aurelianianus marked XXI); temple of Sol Invictus dedicated (25 December); pork added to the dole.
Aurelian murdered at Caenophrurium in Thrace (autumn); an interregnum; Tacitus chosen.
Tacitus dies at Tyana; Florianus briefly; Probus accedes. Major Frankish and Alamannic invasion of Gaul (275-276).
Probus restores the Rhine frontier; resettles Bastarnae and others in Thrace.
Usurpations of Proculus and Bonosus at Cologne; Saturninus in the East.
Probus murdered at Sirmium by soldiers set to drain marshes; Carus accedes and makes his sons Carinus and Numerian Caesars.
Carus takes Ctesiphon and dies there (struck by lightning, per the sources).

Numerian found dead in his litter near Nicomedia; Diocletian proclaimed (20 November) and kills the prefect Aper; takes the consulship with Bassus. Era of Diocletian (Era of the Martyrs) counted from 29 August 284.
Diocletian's party dated by Diocletian II and Aristobulus. Carinus defeated or murdered at the Margus (spring); Diocletian sole emperor; Maximian made Caesar (July).
Maximian made Augustus (1 April 286 or 285). Carausius seizes Britain and northern Gaul (286 or 287).
Diocletian takes the name Jovius, Maximian Herculius.
Maximian's naval expedition against Carausius fails.
The Cassius Dio of this year is not the historian.
Both were praetorian prefects.
Tetrarchy: Constantius and Galerius made Caesars (1 March). Constantius takes Boulogne; Carausius murdered by Allectus.
Coinage reform: new silver argenteus, bronze nummus (c. 294-296).
Edict on marriage (incest) of Diocletian. Caesarean rescript on Manichaeans perhaps 302.
Constantius and Asclepiodotus recover Britain (Allectus killed); Arras medallion. Galerius defeated by Narseh near Carrhae (296/297). Egypt's revolt of Domitius Domitianus (297-298).

Galerius defeats Narseh in Armenia and captures his harem. Provincial reform: provinces roughly doubled and grouped into dioceses (c. 297; Verona List c. 303-314). Census-based tax system (iugatio and capitatio).
Peace of Nisibis: five Transtigritane regions ceded to Rome. Siege of Alexandria (297-298).
Purge of Christians from the army begins (c. 299).
Edict on Maximum Prices (late 301) and currency edict of Aphrodisias (1 September 301) retariffing the coinage.
Edict against the Manichaeans (302 or 297).
Great Persecution: first edict (23/24 February) orders churches destroyed and scriptures burned; further edicts 303-304. Vicennalia celebrated in Rome (20 November).
Fourth edict orders universal sacrifice.
Abdication of Diocletian at Nicomedia and Maximian at Milan (1 May); Constantius and Galerius Augusti, Severus and Maximinus Daia Caesars. Diocletian retires to Spalatum.
Constantius dies at Eboracum (25 July); his army proclaims Constantine. Maxentius proclaimed at Rome (28 October).

The fasti split. In Maximian's and Constantine's realm and at Rome, Maximian IX and Constantine; in Galerius' realm Severus II and Maximinus Caesar were proclaimed (Severus was captured and killed by Maxentius), after which the East used other formulae. Constantine marries Fausta.

Diocletian X and Galerius VII in the East (and briefly in Constantine's territory); in Maxentius' Rome, post-consular dating until April, then Maxentius and his son Romulus. Conference of Carnuntum (November): Licinius made Augustus.
Licinius and Constantine in the territories of Galerius and Constantine; Maxentius II and Romulus II in Italy and Africa. Romulus dies (309).
Andronicus and Probus in the East; Maxentius III alone in Italy. Maximian's revolt and death at Massilia.

In the East Galerius VIII and Maximinus II. Maxentius' territory used post-consular dating and then consuls of his own whose names are disputed. Galerius' edict of toleration (30 April) shortly before his death.
Maxentius IV in Rome until his death at the Milvian Bridge (28 October). Constantine's vision (Lactantius: the chi-rho on shields; Eusebius: the sign in the sky).

Maximinus Daia used Maximinus III in his territory until his defeat by Licinius at Campus Ergenus (30 April) and death at Tarsus. Licinius' letter on toleration (the 'Edict of Milan', June 313). Donatist schism; Council of Rome.
Council of Arles. First war between Constantine and Licinius (Cibalae, 316 or 314).
Arch of Constantine dedicated (decennalia).
Battle of Cibalae (8 October 316 by the now preferred date) and Campus Ardiensis; Licinius cedes the Balkans except Thrace.
Crispus, Constantine II and Licinius II made Caesars (1 March).
Arius' teaching controversial in Alexandria (c. 318).
Licinius' territory appears to have used different formulae from about this time.
Constantine's consuls; Licinius' realm probably used Licinius VI and his son. From 321 to 324 the two halves did not recognise each other's consuls.
Western consuls; the East under Licinius used post-consular or its own dating. Sunday made a legal day of rest (7 March 321).
Western consuls (not recognised by Licinius). Constantine defeats the Sarmatians.
Western consuls (not recognised by Licinius). Constantine's Gothic campaign crosses into Licinius' territory.
Constantine defeats Licinius at Adrianople (3 July) and Chrysopolis (18 September); sole emperor. Constantinople founded (8 November). Constantius made Caesar.

Proculus was removed during the year (his name erased from some inscriptions) and replaced by Julius Julianus. Council of Nicaea (May-July): Arius condemned; homoousios creed; date of Easter. Licinius executed.
Constantine's vicennalia in Rome; execution of Crispus at Pola and then of Fausta. Helena's pilgrimage to Palestine; churches of the Holy Sepulchre and Nativity.
The Constantius of this year is a praetorian prefect, not the emperor's son.
Bridge over the Danube at Oescus. Athanasius bishop of Alexandria.
Dedication of Constantinople (11 May).
Temple treasures confiscated; gold solidus spreads with the proceeds.
Constantine II defeats the Goths (20 April); treaty with the Tervingi. Law tying coloni to the land (CTh 5.17.1).
Constans made Caesar (25 December). Bordeaux Pilgrim's itinerary.

consuls: Amnius Manius Caesonius Nicomachus Anicius Paulinus
fasti.note: Sarmatians resettled within the empire (300,000 per the Origo).
Dalmatius made Caesar. Council of Tyre deposes Athanasius; exiled to Trier. Church of the Holy Sepulchre dedicated.
Tricennalia; death of Arius.
Constantine baptised by Eusebius of Nicomedia; dies near Nicomedia (22 May). Massacre of collateral relatives; his three sons Augusti (9 September).
Shapur II besieges Nisibis (337/338, 346, 350).
Constantine II killed invading Constans' territory near Aquileia.
Dedication Council of Antioch. Ulfila consecrated bishop of the Goths. Law against pagan sacrifice (CTh 16.10.2).
Council of Serdica splits East and West. Constans visits Britain in winter (342/343).
The West initially named Bonosus as colleague of Leontius before Sallustius replaced him.
Second siege of Nisibis.
Battle of Singara (348 or 344). Rome celebrates its 1,100th year; FEL TEMP REPARATIO coinage.
Magnentius usurps at Autun (18 January); Constans killed. Vetranio in Illyricum; Nepotianus at Rome (June).

Constantius' territory used post-consular dating (post consulatum Sergii et Nigriniani); Magnentius named himself and Gaiso. Gallus made Caesar (15 March). Battle of Mursa (28 September), one of the bloodiest of the century.
Magnentius' consuls in his remaining territory.
Magnentius defeated at Mons Seleucus; suicide at Lugdunum (10 August).
Gallus executed at Pola. Chronograph of 354 (Filocalus).

consuls: Quintus Flavius Maesius Egnatius Lollianus Mavortius
fasti.note: Silvanus' usurpation at Cologne (August), suppressed in 28 days. Julian made Caesar (6 November).
Constantius orders the temples closed (CTh 16.10.4).
Constantius' visit to Rome (April-May); obelisk erected in the Circus Maximus; removal of the Altar of Victory. Julian defeats the Alamanni at Strasbourg (August).
Earthquake destroys Nicomedia (24 August).
Councils of Ariminum and Seleucia; homoian creed. Shapur II takes Amida after a 73-day siege (Ammianus 19.1-8).
Julian proclaimed Augustus by his troops at Paris (February/March). Singara and Bezabde fall.
Constantius dies at Mopsucrenae (3 November) en route to fight Julian. Both consuls fled from Julian.
Mamertinus' panegyric on Julian. Julian's school law (17 June) bars Christians from teaching classics; attempt to rebuild the Jerusalem Temple (363). Fire in the temple of Apollo at Daphne.
Julian's Persian expedition; killed in a skirmish near Maranga (26 June). Jovian surrenders Nisibis, Singara and the Transtigritane regions.
Varronianus was Jovian's infant son. Jovian dies at Dadastana (17 February); Valentinian I proclaimed (26 February), makes Valens co-emperor (28 March); division of the army and court at Naissus.
Usurpation of Procopius at Constantinople (28 September). Tsunami in the eastern Mediterranean (21 July).
Gratian was aged seven. Procopius defeated at Thyatira and Nacolia, executed. Damasus bishop of Rome after riots (137 dead in a basilica, Ammianus 27.3).
Gratian made Augustus. 'Barbarian conspiracy' in Britain. Valens' first Gothic war (367-369).
Theodosius the Elder restores Britain (368-369).
Valentinianus Galates was Valens' infant son. Treaty with Athanaric on a boat in the Danube.
Trials for magic and adultery at Rome under Maximinus (369-371).
Treason and magic trials at Antioch (371-372).
Revolt of Firmus in Mauretania (372-375).
Death of Athanasius.
Ambrose made bishop of Milan. Quadi invade Pannonia.

No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Gratiani III et Equitii). Valentinian I dies of a stroke at Brigetio while berating Quadi envoys (17 November); Valentinian II (aged four) proclaimed. Huns attack the Greuthungi.
Valens admits the Tervingi under Fritigern across the Danube. Theodosius the Elder executed at Carthage.
Battle ad Salices, indecisive.
Gratian defeats the Lentienses at Argentaria. Battle of Adrianople (9 August): Valens and two-thirds of the eastern field army killed.
Theodosius made Augustus at Sirmium (19 January). Ausonius' Gratiarum actio for his consulship.
Edict Cunctos populos (Thessalonica, 28 February) defines orthodoxy as the faith of Damasus and Peter of Alexandria.
Council of Constantinople. Athanaric received at Constantinople, dies there.
Treaty with the Goths (3 October): settlement in Thrace as federates under their own leaders. Gratian removes the Altar of Victory and cuts state funds for the pagan cults.
Magnus Maximus proclaimed in Britain; Gratian killed at Lugdunum (25 August). Arcadius made Augustus (19 January).
Symmachus' Relatio III on the Altar of Victory, answered by Ambrose.
Priscillian executed at Trier, the first heretic executed by Christian authority. Augustine's panegyric on Bauto at Milan.
Honorius was aged two (nobilissimus puer). Ambrose resists the court over a basilica for the Arians. Augustine's conversion at Milan.
Riot of the statues at Antioch. Maximus invades Italy; Valentinian II flees to Theodosius. Partition of Armenia with Persia (c. 387).
Magnus Maximus held a consulship of his own in his territory. Maximus defeated at Siscia and Poetovio, executed at Aquileia (28 August).
Theodosius' entry into Rome; Pacatus' panegyric.
Massacre at Thessalonica (some 7,000 killed); Theodosius' penance before Ambrose. Obelisk of Theodosius erected in the Hippodrome.
Theodosian laws banning sacrifice and temple visits (24 February, 16 June). Serapeum of Alexandria destroyed.
Valentinian II found hanged at Vienne (15 May); Arbogast proclaims Eugenius (22 August). Comprehensive ban on pagan cult (CTh 16.10.12, 8 November).
Eugenius, not recognised in the East, was sole consul in his territory. Honorius made Augustus (23 January). Last ancient Olympic Games traditionally dated to 393.
Nicomachus Flavianus named by Eugenius in the West until the Frigidus (5-6 September); Arbogast and Flavianus commit suicide.

The two young sons of Petronius Probus; Claudian's first Latin panegyric. Theodosius dies at Milan (17 January); empire divided between Arcadius (East) and Honorius (West) with Stilicho as guardian. Alaric's Goths revolt; Rufinus murdered (27 November). Huns raid Asia Minor and Syria through the Caucasus.
Alaric ravages Greece; Stilicho's expedition (397) ends inconclusively.

Caesarius nominated in the East, Atticus in the West, the regular pattern after 395. Revolt of Gildo in Africa; he transfers allegiance to Constantinople. Stilicho declared a public enemy by the eastern Senate.
Gildo defeated by his brother Mascezel. Honorius marries Stilicho's daughter Maria. Alaric made magister militum per Illyricum by the East.
Eutropius, the eunuch chamberlain, was the first eunuch consul; the West never recognised him, and he fell in August after Tribigild's revolt (damnatio memoriae). Claudian's In Eutropium.
Gainas' coup at Constantinople; Gothic troops massacred (12 July). Gainas killed by the Hun Uldin.
Fravitta, a pagan Goth, had destroyed Gainas' fleet. Alaric invades Italy (November).
Battle of Pollentia (6 April, Easter) and Verona (summer 402 or 403): Stilicho checks Alaric. Court moves from Milan to Ravenna (by 402).
Theodosius II, aged one, consul for the first time.
Honorius' sixth consulship celebrated in Rome (Claudian's panegyric). Last recorded gladiatorial combat at Rome (Telemachus' martyrdom, Theodoret; date uncertain). John Chrysostom exiled.
Stilicho's second consulship was not recognised in the East, which dated by Anthemius alone. Radagaisus invades Italy (405-406); defeated at Faesulae (23 August 406).
Rhine crossing by Vandals, Alans and Sueves (31 December 406, or 405 on Kulikowski's argument). Usurpations in Britain: Marcus, Gratian.
Constantine III proclaimed in Britain and crosses to Gaul.

Arcadius dies (1 May); Theodosius II aged seven, under the prefect Anthemius. Stilicho executed at Ravenna (22 August); massacre of barbarian soldiers' families. Alaric's first siege of Rome; ransom of 5,000 pounds of gold and 30,000 of silver.

Constantine III recognised by Honorius as colleague and consul in his realm (Honorius VIII and Constantine). Alaric's second siege; Priscus Attalus proclaimed emperor by the Senate. Vandals, Alans and Sueves enter Spain (28 September or 13 October).

Tertullus was the consul of the usurper Attalus and recognised only in Rome; Honorius' court recognised Varanes. Sack of Rome by Alaric (24-27 August). Death of Alaric in Bruttium. 'Rescript of Honorius' to Britain (Zosimus 6.10), possibly to Bruttium.
The West named no consul and used post-consular dating. Constantius (III) defeats Constantine III at Arles; Jovinus proclaimed in Gaul. Conference of Carthage against the Donatists.
Athaulf leads the Goths into Gaul.
Heraclianus, comes Africae, revolted and invaded Italy; defeated, executed and his consulship annulled. The East dated by Lucius. Augustine begins the City of God (413-426).
Athaulf marries Galla Placidia at Narbo (January 414). Attalus again proclaimed by the Goths.
Hypatia murdered at Alexandria (March 415). Athaulf murdered at Barcelona; Wallia succeeds.
Treaty of Constantius with Wallia: Placidia returned for 600,000 measures of grain; Goths fight Vandals and Alans in Spain.
Constantius marries Galla Placidia (1 January). Rutilius Namatianus' De reditu suo (417).
Visigoths settled in Aquitania Secunda with Toulouse as base. Council of the Seven Provinces at Arles revived.
Both eastern nominees, recognised in the West.
Roman-Persian war (420-422).
Constantius made Augustus (8 February) but not recognised by Constantinople; dies 2 September. Theodosius II marries Eudocia (Athenais).
Peace with Persia; freedom of worship for Christians in Persia and Zoroastrians in Rome. Payments to the Huns begin (350 pounds of gold, rising later).
Honorius dies at Ravenna (15 August); the primicerius notariorum John usurps in the West.
Castinus was named by the usurper John and not recognised by the East or later. Eastern expedition under Ardabur and Aspar against John.

John captured at Ravenna and executed at Aquileia. Valentinian III (aged six) made Augustus at Rome (23 October); Placidia regent. Aetius brings 60,000 Huns (Philostorgius) too late, bought off. University of Constantinople (the 'Capitol') founded (27 February 425).
Law of Citations names Papinian, Paul, Ulpian, Modestinus and Gaius as authorities (CTh 1.4.3, 7 November 426).
Revolt of Boniface in Africa; expedition against him.
Nestorius bishop of Constantinople. Gaiseric becomes king of the Vandals.
Vandals cross to Africa (May); 80,000 by Victor of Vita's count. Commission for the Theodosian Code (renewed 435).
Augustine dies during the Vandal siege of Hippo (28 August). Aetius kills the magister militum Felix.
Council of Ephesus (Theotokos); Nestorius deposed. Whether this Bassus is the consul of 408 iterating or a namesake is disputed.
Boniface defeats Aetius near Ariminum, dies of wounds; Aetius flees to the Huns. Patrick's mission to Ireland (traditional date).
Aetius returns with Hunnic support and becomes magister utriusque militiae and patrician (433-435).
Attila and Bleda succeed Ruga (c. 434-435).
Treaty of Hippo (11 February) settles the Vandals in Numidia and Mauretania. Treaty of Margus doubles Hun tribute to 700 pounds.
Both apparently eastern nominees. Aetius' Hunnic auxiliaries destroy the Burgundian kingdom at Worms (436-437), the basis of the Nibelung legend.
Both western nominees. Valentinian III marries Licinia Eudoxia at Constantinople (29 October).
Theodosian Code promulgated (15 February), in force from 1 January 439; presented to the Senate in Rome (gesta senatus, 25 December 438).
Gaiseric takes Carthage (19 October), ending the 435 treaty.
Vandals raid Sicily. Leo I bishop of Rome.
Cyrus of Panopolis, the poet-prefect who rebuilt the walls and lit Constantinople at night; the West named no consul. Huns attack the Danube cities (Viminacium, Margus, Naissus).
Treaty with Gaiseric recognises Vandal control of the richest African provinces (Byzacena, Proconsularis, eastern Numidia).
Paterius' origin is uncertain. Burgundians resettled in Sapaudia. Anatolius' treaty with Attila: arrears of 6,000 pounds and 2,100 per year.
Valentinian III's novel against Pelagians and Manichaeans; western fiscal crisis (Nov. Val. 15 on the siliquaticum, 444/445).
Attila murders Bleda (c. 445).
Both apparently western nominees. The appeal of the Britons 'to Aetius, thrice consul' (Gildas, De excidio 20) is dated 446-454 by the title.
Earthquake throws down the Theodosian walls (26 January); rebuilt in 60 days. Attila's great Balkan campaign; battle of the Utus. Ardabur is the son of Aspar.
Priscus' embassy to Attila (449). Bacaudae in Gaul under Eudoxius.
'Robber Council' (Latrocinium) of Ephesus (August).
Both western nominees. Theodosius II dies after a riding fall (28 July); Pulcheria marries Marcian, who stops tribute to Attila. Honoria's ring offered to Attila. Galla Placidia dies (27 November).

Attila invades Gaul; besieges Orléans; defeated by Aetius and Theodoric I at the Catalaunian Plains (20 June?), where Theodoric I is killed. Council of Chalcedon (October): Christ in two natures; canon 28 on Constantinople's rank.
Attila invades Italy; Aquileia destroyed; turns back after the embassy of Pope Leo, Avienus and Trygetius (and plague and an eastern attack on his homeland).
Attila dies on his wedding night (453); Hunnic empire breaks up after Nedao (454).
Both eastern. The eastern Aetius is a different man. Valentinian III personally murders Aetius on the Palatine at Ravenna (21 or 22 September).

Valentinian III assassinated by Aetius' bucellarii (16 March). Petronius Maximus emperor; killed fleeing (31 May). Vandal sack of Rome (2-16 June); Eudoxia and her daughters taken to Carthage. Avitus proclaimed at Arles (9 July) with Visigothic backing.

Avitus' consulship was not recognised in the East, which named Iohannes and Varanes. Sidonius' panegyric on Avitus (1 January). Ricimer defeats a Vandal fleet off Corsica and deposes Avitus at Placentia (October). Theodoric II defeats the Sueves at the Órbigo.

Both eastern consuls; the West recognised them. Marcian dies (27 January); Leo I proclaimed (7 February) with Aspar's backing, crowned by the patriarch (debated). Majorian proclaimed (1 April or 28 December 457).
Majorian's legislation (Novels) on tax arrears, curiales, defensores, and monuments of Rome.
Majorian recovers Gaul from Theodoric II.
Majorian's invasion fleet of 300 ships destroyed by the Vandals at Portus Ilicitanus (Cartagena area).
Majorian deposed by Ricimer at Dertona (2 August) and executed (7 August). Libius Severus proclaimed (19 November), not recognised by Leo.
Severus' consulship not recognised in the East. Aegidius' breakaway command in northern Gaul (domain of Soissons). Marcellinus in Dalmatia independent.
Battle of Orléans: Aegidius defeats the Visigoths.
Olybrius, later emperor (472), consul in the East. Aegidius dies; Paul and then Syagrius in Soissons.
Both eastern; Hermenericus was a son of Aspar. Libius Severus dies (14 November); interregnum in the West (465-467). Great fire of Constantinople.
Leo III sole consul; any western nomination in the interregnum is not securely attested. Euric murders his brother Theodoric II and becomes Visigothic king.
No western consul. Anthemius proclaimed in the West (12 April) with eastern backing; his daughter marries Ricimer.

Anthemius sole consul (as Augustus, recognised by both courts). The joint East-West expedition against the Vandals under Basiliscus (over 1,000 ships, 64,000 or 120,000 pounds of gold) destroyed by fireships off Cape Bon.
Marcian is Anthemius' son. Arvandus, praetorian prefect of Gaul, tried for treason (letter to Euric).
Euric expands the Visigothic kingdom; Riothamus' Britons defeated at Bourg-de-Déols (469/470).
Aspar and his son Ardabur murdered in the palace at Constantinople. Theodoric (the Amal) begins his career on his return as a hostage.
Ricimer besieges Rome and kills Anthemius (11 July); Olybrius emperor; Ricimer dies (18 August); Olybrius dies (October or November). Gundobad the kingmaker.
West without consuls: Glycerius proclaimed (3 or 5 March) by Gundobad, not recognised by Leo.
Leo II, the infant grandson of Leo I, sole consul. Leo I dies (18 January); Leo II and his father Zeno co-emperors; Leo II dies (November). Julius Nepos deposes Glycerius (June).

Basiliscus seizes Constantinople (January); Zeno flees to Isauria. Orestes expels Nepos from Ravenna and makes his son Romulus Augustus emperor (31 October). Euric gains Auvergne by treaty with Nepos.

Odoacer proclaimed king by the federate troops (23 August); Orestes killed at Placentia (28 August); Romulus Augustulus deposed and pensioned in Campania (4 September); imperial regalia sent to Constantinople. Zeno restored (August). The West named no consuls this year.
No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Basilisci II et Armati) in both halves. Gaiseric dies (25 January).
Illus, the Isaurian general, consul in the East and recognised in Italy.
Zeno sole consul. Revolt of Marcian (son of Anthemius) at Constantinople suppressed.
Odoacer resumes western nominations. Julius Nepos murdered in Dalmatia (9 May); Odoacer annexes Dalmatia (481).
Clovis succeeds Childeric I (481 or 482).
Zeno's Henotikon (482) seeks to reconcile Chalcedonians and Miaphysites; leads to the Acacian schism (484-519) with Rome.
The East named no consul (or it was not recognised in Italy).
Theodoric the Amal consul in the East. Revolt of Illus and Leontius (484-488). Huneric's persecution of Nicene Christians in Africa (conference of Carthage, 1 February 484).
Symmachus, later Boethius' father-in-law.
Clovis defeats Syagrius at Soissons, ending the Roman enclave in northern Gaul.
Father of the philosopher Boethius.
Both consuls named in the West. Zeno commissions Theodoric to invade Italy against Odoacer.
Theodoric defeats Odoacer on the Isonzo (28 August) and at Verona (30 September).
Battle of the Adda (11 August); Odoacer besieged in Ravenna (490-493).
Zeno dies (9 April); Anastasius chosen by the empress Ariadne, who marries him. Isaurian War (492-497).
Both eastern.
Odoacer surrenders Ravenna (5 March) and is killed by Theodoric at a banquet (15 March).
Praesidius' origin is uncertain. Asterius' colophon on the Medicean Virgil records his edition during his consulship.
Clovis defeats the Alamanni (Tolbiac); baptism of Clovis (496, 498 or 508 debated).
Anastasius recognises Theodoric's rule in Italy and returns the palace regalia.
Anastasius abolishes the chrysargyron (collatio lustralis) and introduces the follis coinage reform (498).
Theodoric's visit to Rome (tricennalia); grain distributions and wall repairs.
Laurentian schism at Rome (498-506).
Avienus iunior, son of Faustus Niger, not the consul of 501. Kavadh I invades Roman Mesopotamia; Theodosiopolis (Erzurum) and Amida (January 503) fall.
Anastasian Persian War (502-506).
Amida recovered by purchase (504/505). Theodoric's forces take Sirmium (504).
Dara (Anastasiopolis) fortified on the frontier (505-507).
Breviary of Alaric (Lex Romana Visigothorum) issued (2 February 506).
Clovis defeats and kills Alaric II at Vouillé; the Visigoths lose most of Gaul.
Clovis receives an honorary consulship (codicils) from Anastasius at Tours (Gregory of Tours 2.38). Ostrogoths secure Provence.
Boethius, philosopher, sole consul.
Death of Clovis (27 November); Council of Orléans.
Riots at Constantinople over the Trisagion addition; Anastasius offers to abdicate in the Hippodrome.
Revolt of Vitalian in Thrace (513-515). Clementinus' consular diptych survives (Liverpool).
Cassiodorus, author of the Variae and the Chronica (which ends at 519).
Vitalian's fleet burned by Marinus (with 'sulphur', per Malalas).
The eastern Anastasius was the emperor's grandnephew. Burgundian Council of Epaone.
Anastasius dies (9 July); Justin I, commander of the excubitors, chosen.
Eutharic, Theodoric's son-in-law and designated heir, consul with the emperor as his colleague. End of the Acacian schism (28 March).
Vitalian murdered in the palace (July).
Justinian's consulship games cost 288,000 solidi (Marcellinus comes).
The two sons of Boethius, both named in the West and accepted by Justin as a sign of goodwill; Boethius magister officiorum.
Boethius arrested on a charge of treasonable correspondence with Constantinople; Consolation of Philosophy written in prison.
Boethius executed (524 or 526).
Pope John I sent to Constantinople by Theodoric. Dionysius Exiguus' Easter tables introduce AD dating (525).
Theodoric dies (30 August); Amalasuntha regent for Athalaric. Earthquake destroys Antioch (May 526): 250,000 dead per Malalas.
Justinian co-emperor (1 April); Justin dies (1 August).
Commission for the Codex Justinianus (13 February). Earthquake at Antioch.
First Codex Justinianus (7 April). Academy at Athens loses its funding (529). Samaritan revolt. Benedict at Monte Cassino (traditional).
Both western. Battle of Dara: Belisarius defeats the Persians.
No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Lampadii et Orestis). Battle of Callinicum (Easter). Khosrow I succeeds Kavadh (September).

No consuls: second year after the consulship of Lampadius and Orestes. Nika riot (13-18 January): 30,000 killed in the Hippodrome; Hagia Sophia burned. 'Eternal Peace' with Persia (11,000 pounds of gold).
Digest (16 December) and Institutes (21 November) promulgated. Belisarius conquers the Vandal kingdom: Ad Decimum (13 September), Tricamarum (December).

Decius Paulinus the last western (Italian) consul. Second Codex Justinianus (16 November). Gelimer surrenders; Belisarius' triumph at Constantinople. Athalaric dies; Amalasuntha shares power with Theodahad.
Belisarius consul (sole). Amalasuntha murdered (30 April); Gothic War begins; Belisarius takes Sicily. Volcanic dust veil ('dimmed sun') of 535/536 (Procopius, Cassiodorus).
No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Belisarii). Belisarius takes Naples and enters Rome (9/10 December); Witigis king of the Goths.

No consuls: second year after Belisarius. Witigis besieges Rome (March 537-March 538). Hagia Sophia dedicated (27 December). Justinian's Novel 47 (31 August 537) requires documents to be dated by the regnal year first.
Iohannes the Cappadocian, praetorian prefect, consul.
Apion of the Egyptian landowning family. Franks under Theudebert invade Italy.
Iustinus, son of Germanus. Belisarius takes Ravenna (May); Witigis to Constantinople. Khosrow I sacks Antioch and deports its people to 'Weh Antiok Khosrow'.

Basilius, a Roman aristocrat nominated in the East, was the last ordinary consul; afterwards years were reckoned post consulatum Basilii (counting to p.c. XXV in 566), until Justin II revived the title as part of the imperial office (566). Totila king of the Goths. Plague of Justinian reaches Pelusium (July 541) and Constantinople (spring 542).
